description: Read-only: status of the most recently written journaled run under artifacts/runstate (runbook 1.1). Exit 3 = UNKNOWN, exit 4 = no journaled run yet.
Read-only: pre-journal legacy era discovery via /proc (runbook 1.2). Exit 3 (UNKNOWN) while the wrapper is live; exit 4 after it exits and before the store is adopted.

MUTATES the repo's artifacts tree: /tmp is volatile (one reboot deletes the only copy) — copy the era log the MOMENT the wrapper exits; the launcher has already appended its own ERA_EXIT=<code> line, so verify it with tail -1. Only if that line is missing may you append ERA_EXIT=UNKNOWN by hand — never a guessed code (runbook 4.1). Non-zero ERA_EXIT stops the closeout sequence.
Read-only: compute the capture-manifest content hash to pin in the adopt-pin step (runbook 4.2).

command: closeout: adopt the sealed coverage era
description: MUTATES artifacts/runstate: create the run store from the operator-authored RunIdentity JSON (runbook 4.2). RUN_ID_PLACEHOLDER = the deterministic run id (tree_options.runstate.store.compute_run_id).

command: pre-journal legacy era; journaling the observed lane
description: MUTATES the journal: record the lane as it actually happened — skips are illegal (runbook 4.2).

command: bind the run to the sealed capture manifest
description: MUTATES the journal: pin the manifest hash from the manifest-hash step; --pin-manifest pins INSTEAD of transitioning (runbook 4.2).

command: wrapper ERA_EXIT=0; log copied; manifest pinned
description: MUTATES the journal: close the capture lane (runbook 4.2).

MUTATES artifacts/ only: regenerate the declared universe into a throwaway artifacts path (the byte-compare against the committed file is the NEXT step). Divergence means the era wrapper changed under a declared universe — an incident, never a hand-fix (runbook 1.3).

Read-only: byte-identical regeneration proof — divergence means the era wrapper changed under a declared universe (an incident, never a hand-fix). Burst (cmp non-zero) is the same failure mode the previous step's regenerate catches with its OWN exit code; this step is the explicit comparison. Round-1 review fix.

MUTATES artifacts/census: the typed census of the sealed capture. Exit 0 = whole coverage (holiday-Friday spot gaps are EXPECTED and do not count); exit 5 = emitted but incomplete — owner escalation, never a silent re-run; exit 2 against a mid-run dir is BY DESIGN (runbook 4.3).

MUTATES artifacts/amendment only: owner-gated DRY-RUN proposal — the owner supplies values + ratified rules (the threshold is an owner-ratified input bound to the census hash); every packet lands landed:false (runbook 4.4).

Read-only (preflight is the default): on the live 0.2.2 protocol with no BARS_LAUNCH_APPROVAL record binding its hash, exit 2 on the RECORD clause is the DOCUMENTED correct answer, not a failure to fix (runbook 4.5). After the continuation approval is appended, the documented answer for a continuation launch becomes exit 3 on the census clause (the census stays sealed at the coverage era; see docs/window-a-extension-runbook.md).

Read-only: typed verification of both lane manifests and every referenced payload, clean checkout/protocol, owner calendar artifact, and sealed criteria/source; exit 2 while any artifact is unavailable is expected. g4_seal execute is PROHIBITED in this campaign (runbook 4.6).
